Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:10:1.english: From his own - That he separated [it] from his [own] grain heap.

Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:10:2.hebrew: בין שניתן לו במתנה - קס"ד לאחר שהפריש ניתן לו, וקתני מוסיף חומש, דשלו הוא, וקרינן ביה "אם גאל יגאל איש ממעשרו" (ויקרא כז):
Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:10:2.english: Whether it was given to him as a gift - It enters [our] mind [that] after [the giver] separated [it], it was given to him; and [the mishna] teaches [that he] adds a fifth, because it is his, and we apply to him [the verse]: "If a man will redeem of his tithe" (Leviticus 27:31).

Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:10:3.hebrew: ממון גבוה הוא - ולא מצי יהיב ליה, והוה ליה זה שניתן לו כאילו אינו שלו, ואין מוסיף חומש אלא בעלים, דלא קרינא ביה "ממעשרו":
Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:10:3.english: It is property belonging to the Most High - And [therefore] he cannot give it to him [as a gift], and so for this [person] to whom it was given, it is as though it is not his, and only the owner adds a fifth, since we do not read concerning him: “from his tithe.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:11:1.hebrew: וקסבר כו' - דאיכא למ"ד בעלמא כמי שהורמו דמיין, ואיהו ס"ל: כל זמן שלא הורם, לאו ממון גבוה הוא, דאין שם מעשר עליו לכלום:
Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:11:1.english: And he holds, etc. - For there is an authority elsewhere [who holds that they are] considered as though they have been separated; but he holds [that] as long as it has not been separated, it is not divine property, for the status of tithe does not apply to it at all.

Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:12:1.hebrew: והא גמר קדש קדש - האי תנא גמר ממעשר, דאי לא גמיר, חומש בנטע רבעי מנ"ל? אלמא מעשר נמי ניתן במתנה, ור' יהודה היא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:12:1.english: But didn’t he derive “holy” [from] “holy” - This Tanna derives [the laws of fourth-year produce] from [second] tithe, for if he did not derive [it], from where do we know [the requirement to add] a fifth to fourth-year produce? Consequently, [second] tithe too may be given as a gift, and it is [the opinion of] Rabbi Yehuda.

Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:13:1.hebrew: כשהוא סמדר - כשהענבים ניכרים לאחר שנפל הפרח. וקמ"ל, דכל זמן שהוא סמדר יכול לתתן במתנה, שאין שם רבעי עליו. ודלא כר' יוסי, דאמר במסכת ערלה: סמדר ערלה אסור, מפני שהוא פרי, וקרינא ביה "ערלתו את פריו":
Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:13:1.english: When it is a bud - When the grapes are discernible after the blossom has fallen. And it teaches us that as long as it is a bud, he can give them as a gift, for the status of fourth-year [produce] is not upon it. And [this is] not in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, who said in tractate Orlah: A bud of orlah is forbidden because it is fruit, and we read regarding it: “[and you shall treat] its fruit as forbidden.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:14:1.english: [One] pulled from him - One person from another.

Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:14:2.hebrew: נותן סלע - וקנה את המעשר, שמשעה שמשכו קנאו, ולא אמרינן: ברשות בעליו מעשר אייקר, וצריך לחללו בשנים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:14:2.english: He gives a sela - And he has acquired the tithe, for from the time that he pulled it, he acquired it; and we do not say [that] in the possession of its [original] owner the tithe appreciated, and he must [therefore] redeem it for two [selas].

Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:14:3.english: Because [the] second tithe is his - For the tithe is common property and is acquired by pulling.

Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:14:4.hebrew: ונתן הכסף וקם לו - אין הקדש נקנה במשיכה, דכתיב ביה: ״ויסף חמישית כסף ערכך עליו וקם לו״, ואין שטר וחזקה קונין קרקעותיו, ולא משיכה את מטלטלין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:14:4.english: “And he will give the money and it will be assured to him” - Consecrated property is not acquired through pulling [meshikhah], as it is written concerning it: “And he shall add a fifth of the money of your valuation unto it, and it will be assured to him” (Leviticus 27:19); and neither a deed nor [an act of] possession acquire its land, nor [does] pulling [acquire its] movable property.

Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:15:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן לעולם ר' יהודה והכא חד סתמא והתם תרי סתמי - כר"מ סתם לן תרי זמני. בשתי מקומות תנא רבי משנה זו דכרם רבעי: חדא בסדר זרעים (מעשר שני פ"ה מ"ג), וחדא בעדיות (פ"ד מ"ה):
Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:15:1.english: This is the reading: "Actually, [it is] Rabbi Yehuda, and here [there is] one unattributed [mishna], and there [there are] two unattributed [mishnayot]" - In accordance with Rabbi Meir, [Rebbi] taught anonymously for us twice; in two places Rebbi taught this mishna of a fourth-year vineyard: one in Seder Zera'im (Ma'aser Sheni 5:3), and one in Eduyyot (4:5).

Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:16:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן - ואי סתמא דוקא, מה לי חד סתמא כו':
Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:16:1.english: This is how we read: "And if an unattributed [mishna] is specific, what difference is there to me [between] one unattributed [mishna], etc."

Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:16:2.hebrew: הואיל ותנן בבחירתא כוותיה - מסכת עדיות קרי בחירתא, שכל דבריהם העידו מפי הגדולים, והלכה כמותן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:16:2.english: Since we learned in beḥirata in accordance with his [opinion] - [The Gemara] calls Tractate Eduyyot beḥirata [the select tractate], for all of their statements were testified from the mouth of the great [sages], and the halakha is in accordance with them.

Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:1:1.hebrew: תרי תנאי ואליבא דר' יהודה - איכא למ"ד: ירושלים מקדשא כהקדש, שאם יטול מאבני החומה לבנות בביתו — מעל; ואיכא למ"ד: לא מקדשא. בר פדא פליג אדרב, וס"ל כר' יוחנן, דטעמא דר"מ במתני' משום דקסבר: אין הקדש מתחלל בשוגג, דמקח טעות הוא, דלא ניחא ליה דנתחלל הקדש על ידיה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:1:1.english: [They are] two tanna’im, and according to Rabbi Yehuda - There is one who says: Jerusalem was sanctified like consecrated property, such that if one takes from the stones of the wall to build in his house, he has committed sacrilege; and there is one who says: It was not sanctified. Bar Padda disagrees with Rav and holds in accordance with Rabbi Yochanan, that the reason of Rabbi Meir in the Mishnah is because he maintains: Consecrated property is not desacralized unwittingly, for it is an erroneous transaction, as it is not pleasing to him that consecrated property should be desacralized through him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:2:1.hebrew: ולא אמרו בשוגג מתחלל - כלומר, לא כתיב בתורה מתחלל, אלא שצריך קרבן מעילה; אבל המעות, כל מקום שהולכות — הקדש הם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:2:1.english: And they did not say [that] unwittingly it is desacralized - That is to say, it is not written in the Torah [that it is] desacralized, but rather that one requires a guilt-offering for misappropriation; but the money, wherever it goes, is consecrated.

Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:3:1.hebrew: לענין אכילה - האוכל ככר של הקדש, דאזל ליה הקדש, וה"ה להדלקת נר ולכל הנאה. אבל הוצאת מעות הקדש — אין בהם מעילה, דלא נפקי מרשות הקדש:
Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:3:1.english: With regard to eating - [This refers to] one who eats a loaf of consecrated [bread], for the consecrated [item] is gone; and the same applies to lighting a lamp and to any [such] benefit. But [as for] spending consecrated coins, there is no [liability for] misuse regarding them, for they have not left the domain of the sanctuary.

Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:4:1.english: With regard to [second] tithe - That it is property of Heaven.

Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:4:2.hebrew: כר' יהודה בהקדש - דשוגג מתחלל, ולא מזיד:
Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:4:2.english: In accordance with Rabbi Yehuda with regard to consecrated property - That [if misused] unwittingly, it is desacralized, but not intentionally.

Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:5:1.hebrew: אין לו חומש - המחלל פירותיו להעלות הדמים לירושלים, אין צריך להוסיף חומש, ואפי' בעליו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:5:1.english: It does not have a fifth - One who redeems its fruit to bring the money up to Jerusalem does not need to add a fifth, even its owner.

Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:5:2.hebrew: אין לו ביעור - בשנה שלישית וששית של שמיטה, שהמעשרות מתבערים מן הבית, שאסור להשהותן יותר, כדכתיב: "כי תכלה לעשר" וגו':
Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:5:2.english: It does not have [the law of] disposal - In the third and sixth years of the Sabbatical cycle, when the tithes are removed from the house, as it is forbidden to retain them any longer, as it is written: "When you finish tithing..." etc.

Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:5:3.english: It does have - As [the Gemara] derives below.

Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:6:1.hebrew: יש לו דין פרט ויש לו דין עוללות - דכרמך קרינא ביה, והעניים אוכלין אותן בירושלים, או פודין אותן ומעלין דמיהן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:6:1.english: It has the law of peret [individual fallen grapes] and it has the law of olelot [incompletely formed clusters] - For "your vineyard" applies to it, and the poor eat them in Jerusalem, or redeem them and bring up their value [to Jerusalem].

Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:6:2.hebrew: פרט - הנושר בשעת בצירה, וכתיב (ויקרא י״ט:י׳): "ופרט כרמך לא תלקט":
Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:6:2.english: Fallen grapes [peret] - That which falls off at the time of harvesting; and it is written (Leviticus 19:10): “And you shall not gather the fallen grapes of your vineyard.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:6:3.hebrew: עוללות - אשכול שאין לו פסיגין, אלא אחת היא כולה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:6:3.english: Incompletely formed clusters [olelot] - A cluster that has no branchlets, but rather is entirely a single [stem].

Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:6:4.hebrew: כולו לגת - דקסברי: כולו ממון גבוה הוא, כמעשר שני — דיליף מיניה כדמפרש ואזיל — ולא קרינא ביה כרמך:
Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:6:4.english: All of it [goes] to the winepress - For they hold [that] all of it is property of Heaven, like second tithe — from which it is derived, as [the Gemara] goes on to explain — and we do not read concerning it "your vineyard."

Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:7:1.hebrew: והא גמר קדש קדש - האי תנא גמר ממעשר, דאי לא גמיר, חומש בנטע רבעי מנ"ל? אלמא מעשר נמי ניתן במתנה, ור' יהודה היא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:7:1.english: And didn’t he derive “holy” [from] “holy” - This tanna derives [the laws of fourth-year produce] from [second] tithe, for if he did not derive [it], from where do we [know that there is an addition of a] fifth for fourth-year produce? Evidently, [second] tithe may also be given as a gift, and [the mishna] is [in accordance with] Rabbi Yehuda.

Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:8:1.hebrew: וב"ה - דמדמו כרם רבעי למעשר, כמאן סבירא להו במעשר — לענין ממון גבוה או ממון הדיוט:
Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:8:1.english: And Beit Hillel - Who compare a fourth-year vineyard to [second] tithe — in accordance with whose opinion do they hold regarding [second] tithe, with respect to [whether it is] property of the Most High or common property?

Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:8:2.hebrew: אלא לאו כר"מ - וב"ה כסתם משנה חשיב להו, דהלכה כמותן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:8:2.english: Rather, is it not in accordance with Rabbi Meir - And [Rav Naḥman] considers [the opinion of] Beit Hillel like an unattributed mishna, since the halakha is in accordance with them.

Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:9:1.hebrew: וכר' יהודה בהקדש מאי היא - היכן תנן: בשוגג מתחלל, במזיד אין מתחלל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:9:1.english: And [in accordance with] Rabbi Yehuda regarding consecrated property, what is it? - Where did we learn [that] unwittingly it is desacralized, [whereas] intentionally it is not desacralized?

Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:9:2.hebrew: שילח ביד פיקח - רישא הכי תנן: שלח ביד חרש, שוטה, וקטן — עשו שליחותן, גזבר מעל; לא עשו שליחותן, לא מעל. שלח ביד פיקח, ונזכר עד שלא הגיע אצל חנוני. ואוקמינן התם: כשהוזכרו שניהם — גיזבר ושליח:
Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:9:2.english: [If] he sent by the hand of a competent person - In the first clause [of that mishnah], this is what we learned: [If] he sent [consecrated money] by the hand of a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor — [if] they performed their agency, the treasurer has committed misuse [of consecrated property]; [if] they did not perform their agency, he has not committed misuse. [And the latter clause states: If] he sent [it] by the hand of a competent person, and he remembered before [the agent] reached the storekeeper... And we established there [in Tractate Me'ilah that this refers to a case] where both of them had remembered — the treasurer and the agent.

Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:9:3.hebrew: חנוני מעל כשיוציא - דשגגה גביה איתיה, אבל הני מזידין נינהו ולא מחייבי מעילה. אלמא: שוגג מתחלל, מזיד אין מתחלל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 54b:9:3.english: The storekeeper has committed misuse when he spends [it] - For inadvertence is with him, but these [the sender and the agent] are intentional and are not liable for misuse. Evidently, [consecrated property used] unwittingly becomes deconsecrated, [but when used] intentionally, it does not become deconsecrated.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 54b:1:1.hebrew: תרי תנאי ואליבא דר' יהודה - פ"ה: איכא למ"ד ירושלים מקדשא, שאם יטול מאבני החומה לבנותם בביתו — מעל; ואיכא למ"ד לא מקדשא. מיהו קשה, דבפ' שני דייני גזירות (כתובות דף קו:) תני: אבני מזבח וההיכל והעזרה באין מבדק הבית; חוץ לחומת העזרה, כגון חומת העיר, באין משירי לשכה. ובמסכת שקלים (דף ז.) תניא: אבני מזבח וההיכל והעזרות משירי הלשכה; חוץ לחומת העזרה, כגון חומת העיר, באים מלשכת בדק הבית. וי"ל דבהא פליגי: דההיא דשני דייני גזירות ס"ל אין מועלין בשירים, וכמאן דאמר ירושלים אינה קדושה; והכי קאמר: דאבני מזבח וההיכל והעזרות דקדושים באין מבדק הבית דקדוש כמו כן, וחומת העיר דאינו קדוש בא משירי הלשכה. וההיא דמסכת שקלים דקאמר אבני מזבח וההיכל והעזרה באין משירי לשכה — סבר דמועלין בשירי הלשכה, ולכך עושין מהן דבר קדושה, וכ"ש מבדק הבית דקדיש טפי; חוץ לחומת העזרה, כגון חומות העיר ומגדלותיה, באין מבדק הבית — כלומר: אף מבדק הבית דקדוש קדושה גדולה, דקסבר ירושלים קדשה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 54b:1:1.english: "They are two tanna’im, and according to Rabbi Yehuda" - Rashi explained: There is one authority who holds that Jerusalem was sanctified, so that if one takes stones from the wall [of the city] to build them into his house, he has committed me’ilah; and there is one authority who holds that it was not sanctified. However, this is difficult, for in the chapter [entitled] "Shenei Dayyanei Gezeirot" (Ketubot 106b) it teaches [in a baraita]: The stones of the altar, the Sanctuary, and the Courtyard come from Bedek HaBayit (the Temple maintenance fund); [materials for anything] outside the Courtyard wall, such as the city wall, come from the surplus of the chamber (sheyarei halishkah). And in tractate Shekalim (7a) it is taught: The stones of the altar, the Sanctuary, and the Courtyards [come] from the surplus of the chamber; [materials for anything] outside the Courtyard wall, such as the city wall, come from the chamber of Bedek HaBayit. And it can be said that they disagree about this: that that [baraita] of "Shenei Dayyanei Gezeirot" holds that me’ilah does not apply to the surplus [of the chamber], and [it is] in accordance with the one who says [in our Gemara] that Jerusalem was not sanctified; and this is what it is saying: that the stones of the altar, the Sanctuary, and the Courtyards, which are holy, come from Bedek HaBayit, which is likewise holy; and the city wall, which is not holy, comes from the surplus of the chamber. And that [baraita] of tractate Shekalim which states that the stones of the altar, the Sanctuary, and the Courtyard come from the surplus of the chamber holds that me’ilah does apply to the surplus of the chamber, and therefore they make sacred items from them, and all the more so [could they come] from Bedek HaBayit, which is even more holy; [and as for the clause,] "[anything] outside the Courtyard wall, such as the walls of the city and its towers, comes from Bedek HaBayit" — meaning, [they may be funded] even from Bedek HaBayit, which is consecrated with great sanctity, for he holds that Jerusalem was sanctified.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 54b:2:1.hebrew: קרבן מי מחייב - דלא היה חייב בהוצאה, אלא באכילה או בהנאת הגוף:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 54b:2:1.english: "Is he liable [to bring] an offering?" - For he would not be liable for expenditure, but only for eating or for bodily benefit.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 54b:3:1.hebrew: לא אמרו אלא לענין אכילה - הא דנקט אכילה לאו דוקא, דה"ה אם היה שמן דהקדש והדליק בו הנר — דמעל, שהרי כילה אותם מן העולם. וא"ת: א"כ, אמאי מועלין בחדתין? וי"ל: דהתם נמי איירי ששקל כנגדן משקולות, שנהנה מגוף השקלים, והוי כמו אכילה; ולא אתא אלא למעוטי הוצאה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 54b:3:1.english: They said [it is desacralized] only with regard to eating - That which it formulated [the rule with] "eating" is not meant exclusively, as the same applies if it was consecrated oil and he kindled the lamp with it, that he has committed me'ilah, for he has consumed it from the world. And if you say: If so, why is one liable for me'ilah with new [shekels]? One can say: There, too, it is dealing with a case where he weighed weights against them [using the coins as counterweights], so that he derived benefit from the substance of the shekels, and [thus] it is like eating; and [the statement] came only to exclude expenditure.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 54b:7:1.hebrew: גמר קדש קדש ממעשר - וא"ת: א"כ, ל"ל "הלולים", דדריש מיניה בפ ' כיצד מברכין (ברכות דף לה.) "אחליה והדר אכליה"? תיפוק ליה מהך ג"ש! וי"ל: דאי מג"ש, לא הוה ידעינן דפדיון רבעי נוהג אלא בזמן שמעשר שני נוהג, ולא בשנה שלישית. אי נמי, ה"א: מאי חזית דגמר ממעשר? נילף משביעית, שתופס דמיו ואינו יוצא לחולין (אבל מאחר דגמרי מהלולים שאינו תופש דמיו, גמר ממעשר):
Tosafot on Kiddushin 54b:7:1.english: [Beit Hillel] derives "holy" "holy" from [second] tithe - And if you say: If so, why do I need [the word] hillulim, from which [the Gemara] expounds in the chapter [entitled] Keitzad Mevarekhin (Berakhot 35a), "Deconsecrate it and then eat it"? Let him derive it from this gezeirah shavah! And one can say: Because if [it were derived only] from the gezeirah shavah, we would not have known that the redemption of fourth-year [produce] applies except at a time when second tithe applies, and not in the third year [of the Sabbatical cycle]. Alternatively, I would have said: What did you see [that leads you] to derive [it] from [second] tithe? Let us derive [it] from Sabbatical year [produce], which grasps its redemption money and does not depart to non-sacred status! (However, once we derive from hillulim that it does not grasp its redemption money [in this manner], [Beit Hillel] derives [the remaining laws] from [second] tithe).

Tosafot on Kiddushin 54b:8:1.hebrew: לעיל לא אמרו אלא לענין אכילה - הא דנקט אכילה לאו דוקא, דה"ה אם היה שמן דהקדש והדליק בו הנר — דמעל, שהרי כילה אותם מן העולם. וא"ת: א"כ, אמאי מועלין בחדתין? וי"ל: דהתם נמי איירי ששקל כנגדן משקולות, שנהנה מגוף השקלים, והוי כמו אכילה; ולא אתא אלא למעוטי הוצאה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 54b:8:1.english: Earlier, "they did not say [it is desacralized unwittingly] except with regard to eating" - That which [the Gemara] stated "eating" is not meant specifically, for the same applies if it was consecrated oil and one kindled a lamp with it, that he has committed misuse, as he completely consumed it from the world. And if you say: If so, why is one liable for misuse with new [shekels]? And one can say: There, too, it is dealing with [a case where] he weighed weights against them, where he derived benefit from the physical substance of the shekels, and it is [thus] like eating; and [the statement] came only to exclude expenditure [of money].

Tosafot on Kiddushin 54b:9:1.hebrew: שילח ביד פיקח ונזכר כו' - וא"ת: אמאי לא מייתי מרישא, דקאמר: "שילח ביד חרש שוטה וקטן, עשו שליחותו — גזבר מעל, לא עשו שליחותו — חנוני מעל", אלמא היכא דהוי שוגג חייב קרבן מעילה? וי"ל: דמההיא לא מוכח אלא דבשוגג מתחלל, אבל דבמזיד לא מתחלל — לא שמעינן; ומהך דהכא שמעינן תרי: מדקאמר "נזכר עד שלא הגיע אצל חנוני, חנוני מעל" — ולא בעל הבית — אלמא משמע דבמזיד אינו מתחלל, ומדקאמר "חנוני מעל לכשיוציא" — מכלל דבשוגג מתחלל:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 54b:9:1.english: [If] he sent [it] in the possession of a competent person and remembered, etc. - And if you say: Why does [the Gemara] not bring [proof] from the first clause [of the mishna], which states: "[If] he sent [it] in the possession of a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor — [if] they performed his agency, the treasurer has committed trespass; [if] they did not perform his agency, the storekeeper has committed trespass"? Thus, wherever [one acts] unwittingly, he is liable [to bring] a trespass offering! And one can say: From that [clause], it is only proven that through an unwitting [act] it is deconsecrated, but that through an intentional [act] it is not deconsecrated, we do not learn. And from this [clause] here, we learn both [points]: from the fact that it states: "[If] he remembered before [the agent] reached the storekeeper, the storekeeper has committed trespass" — and not the homeowner — it implies that through an intentional [act] it is not deconsecrated; and from the fact that it states: "the storekeeper has committed trespass when he spends [it]," it follows that through an unwitting [act] it is deconsecrated.
